options.label: To think about the long term

strong.text: With a strong chart, you love with conviction and a clear picture of what a good relationship looks like. You're a rock for your partner. The note is to leave room for their picture too. Ask once a season: 'What would make this year better for you?' and actually change something based on the answer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Once a season, ask what would make their year better. Then change something.

weak.text: With a weak chart, you love with sensitivity and devotion, and you can lose track of your own needs inside the relationship. Keep a short private list of what makes you feel loved, and share one item a month. Partners can't meet needs they've never heard.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Share one thing from your 'feel loved' list each month.

wood.heading: Your element in love: Wood
wood.text: Wood in love is growth. You want a relationship that's going somewhere, getting deeper, building a future. You're generous and principled, and you grow toward the people you love. Stagnation scares you more than conflict. Talk about your future together often; it reassures you more than you'd admit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood in love: you need to feel it's growing.

fire.heading: Your element in love: Fire
fire.text: Fire in love is warmth and passion. You light up when you're loved and you give affection freely. You want romance to stay alive, not fade into routine. You need a partner who responds with warmth; coldness dims you quickly. Keep the sparks deliberate: date nights, surprises, compliments.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire in love: keep the sparks deliberate.

earth.heading: Your element in love: Earth
earth.text: Earth in love is stability and care. You're loyal, nurturing and dependable. You build homes and keep them warm. You value consistency over drama. Make sure your partner sees your care; Earth's love is so steady it can become invisible.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth in love: so steady it can turn invisible. Say it.

metal.heading: Your element in love: Metal
metal.text: Metal in love is loyalty and integrity. You're committed, honest and protective. You keep promises and expect them kept. You can seem reserved; your feelings run deep but you express them carefully. A partner who earns your trust has it for life.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal in love: trust earned, trust for life.

water.heading: Your element in love: Water
water.text: Water in love is depth and intuition. You understand your partner on levels they didn't know existed. You need emotional and intellectual connection, and some freedom. Possessiveness pushes you away. Give your partner glimpses of your inner world; Water can be hard to read.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water in love: deep. Let them see some of the depths.

gap-wood.text:
Gap Wood rarely asks for reassurance, so partners assume you don't need it. You do. The sentence that lands deepest for you is some version of 'I've got this one, you can rest.' Pines stand up straight all day. Being told you can lean for an hour feels like a holiday.

What doesn't work: praise for being strong. You've heard it your whole life and it quietly adds to the load. Try asking your partner for specific relief instead of general support. 'Can you handle the call with the landlord this week?' is a love request in pine language. And when they say 'I'm proud of you', don't deflect with a joke. Stand there and let it land, the way a tree takes rain.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pines rarely ask. Ask for relief by name this week.

gap-wood.heading: What you need to hear

eul-wood.text:
Eul Wood needs to hear that it's chosen, again and again, in small ways. 'I thought of you when I saw this' does more for you than a dramatic declaration. Vines grow toward what they trust will still be there tomorrow, and little signs of attention are how you check the wall is still standing.

The thing you rarely say is how much you notice when those signs stop. A partner who gets busy and forgets the good-morning text for a week might not even register it. You registered it on day two. Instead of quietly withdrawing, say it lightly: 'I miss the silly texts.' That's not needy. That's a vine telling the gardener where the support has come loose. Most partners are glad to be told.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You notice on day two. Say so lightly, before day ten.

eul-wood.heading: What you need to hear

byeong-fire.text:
Byeong Fire needs to hear that it's enjoyed, not just tolerated. You bring the energy, the plans, the noise, and somewhere inside you wonders if it's too much. The sentence that settles you is 'I love how loud our life is with you.' The sun likes knowing the garden is glad it came up.

Your blind spot is assuming everyone shines the way you do. A quieter partner might show delight with a small smile you missed while telling a story. Watch their face more than their words for a week. And when you're the one who needs comfort, which happens more than people think, say so plainly. 'I need you to be the sunny one tonight' is a fair request. Even the sun gets cloudy days.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The sun relaxes when it knows the noise is wanted.

byeong-fire.heading: What you need to hear

jeong-fire.text:
Jeong Fire needs to hear that the small things were seen. The ticket you remembered, the soup you brought, the joke you planted in their bag. You give care in tiny precise acts, and the quiet fear is that tiny means invisible. 'I saw what you did there' is the sentence that makes a candle burn brighter.

You also need protection from drafts. Harsh words, a cold tone, a door closed too hard: they flicker you more than they would a bigger fire. Let your partner know which kind of conflict you can handle and which kind shakes you. 'You can disagree with me, but please don't go cold' is a reasonable rule. Candles light whole rooms. They just need someone who doesn't open every window at once.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Disagreement is fine. Coldness is the draft that flickers you.

jeong-fire.heading: What you need to hear

mu-earth.text:
Mu Earth needs to hear that it's more than useful. Partners lean on you for decisions, logistics and calm, and they often say thank you for exactly that. Lovely. But the sentence that reaches you is 'I'd want you around even if you never fixed anything.' Mountains get admired for their usefulness and loved for their view.

You won't ask for affection directly, so it helps to build it into routine: a fixed evening walk, a lazy Sunday breakfast, a standing date nobody cancels. Structure is how a mountain says yes to softness. And when your partner wants to talk about feelings, resist the urge to solve. Ask 'Do you want advice or company?' Most of the time they want the mountain to just sit there with them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask: 'Advice or company?' Usually they want the mountain to sit.

mu-earth.heading: What you need to hear

gi-earth.text:
Gi Earth needs to hear that it's allowed to be looked after. You feed, remember, organize and soothe. Partners love it and slowly start to expect it. The sentence that undoes you is 'Sit down, I'm making dinner tonight.' Gardens grow everyone else's food. They rarely get watered back without asking.

So ask, in a garden voice: specific, practical, small. 'Can you plan Saturday? I want to be surprised.' 'Can you do the morning with the dog this week?' You'll feel guilty for about a minute. Then you'll feel rested, and the relationship will get better, because a gardener who's always tired eventually resents the garden. Being cared for isn't taking. It's how the soil stays rich enough to keep giving.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: 'Can you plan Saturday?' Feel guilty for a minute. Then rest.

gi-earth.heading: What you need to hear

gyeong-metal.text:
Gyeong Metal needs to hear that its honesty is welcome. You say what you think, and you've had partners who called it harsh, cold or too much. The sentence that softens you is 'I always know where I stand with you, and I love that.' A sword relaxes when it isn't treated as a threat.

What you need in return is the same directness. Hints exhaust you. A partner who says 'I'm upset because you forgot' gets your full, fair attention. A partner who goes quiet and hopes you'll guess gets a confused sword. Tell them early: 'Please just tell me. I'd rather hear it plainly.' Then hold up your side, which is saying the hard thing with one soft sentence first. Sharp and gentle can live in the same mouth.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: 'Please just tell me plainly.' Then say your hard things gently.

gyeong-metal.heading: What you need to hear

sin-metal.text:
Sin Metal needs to hear that it's valued for more than how it looks or how well it does things. Partners often fall for the polish: the style, the taste, the competence. The sentence that reaches the real you is 'I like you most when you're tired and grumpy.' Jewels want to be loved in the drawer too, not just under the shop lights.

You also need reassurance that mistakes won't end things. Your inner critic already marks every slip. A partner who says 'That was a bad day, not a bad you' gives you something no compliment can. In return, practice being seen unpolished: the messy hair, the bad mood, the half-finished idea. Every time you show it and nothing breaks, the jewel gets a little less afraid of scratches.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: 'A bad day, not a bad you.' That's the sentence you need.

sin-metal.heading: What you need to hear

im-water.text:
Im Water needs to hear that it can leave and come back. Not leave the relationship. Leave the room, the city, the conversation for a while, to think. The sentence that relaxes you is 'Go, have your adventure, tell me everything when you're home.' Oceans stay when the shore doesn't try to hold them.

What you rarely admit is how much the coming back matters. The light left on, the message waiting, the partner who asks a real question about where your mind went. Ask for that. 'When I'm back, ask me about it' is a fair request. And give the same in return: when your partner shares something small, dive in with real curiosity. Depth is your gift. Spend some of it on their everyday stories too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: 'Go, then tell me everything.' That's the shore you stay for.

im-water.heading: What you need to hear

gye-water.text:
Gye Water needs to hear that its feelings make sense. You notice moods, shifts and unspoken things before anyone else, and partners sometimes say you're overthinking. The sentence that settles you is 'You're right, something was off. Thanks for noticing.' Rain is gentler when the ground doesn't argue with it.

You also need lightness. Long serious talks can drown you as much as silence can. A partner who makes you laugh in the middle of a worry is doing real care. Ask for it: 'Can you just distract me for an hour?' And protect your private corner, the journal, the solo walk, the playlist, without explaining it. Mist needs space to drift. It always comes back softer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: 'You're right, something was off.' Rain calms when it's believed.

gye-water.heading: What you need to hear

base.how-you-love:
Gap Wood loves like a tall pine stands: upright, protective and in it for decades. When you commit, you commit to the whole person and the whole future. You're the partner who shows up with soup when they're sick, fixes the leaking tap, remembers the anniversary and plans the next five years in a notebook nobody asked for.

Your love language is reliability. You say 'I love you' by being there, again and again, in the same steady way. You also need respect. A partner who mocks your principles or treats your plans as a joke hurts you more than they realize, because your sense of self is built on standing for something.

The soft spot nobody sees: you want to be looked after too, and you rarely ask. Pines give shade all day and quietly hope someone notices the roots need water.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The tall pine in love: steady for decades.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: A five-year plan in a notebook. Nobody asked. Very romantic, honestly.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Reliability is your love letter.

spring.intro:
You're Wood born in spring, a young tree in a forest that is all growing at once. Element match: the {season} season carries your own element, so you come into love with a strong sense of who you are. You don't dissolve into a partner. That's healthy, and it means the person you choose has to make room for a whole person, habits, opinions, friends and all. You do best with someone equally solid.

For Gap Wood in a relationship, this season shapes how quickly you commit and how much shade you give before you ask for any back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You arrive in love fully formed. Your partner needs room for that.

summer.intro:
Wood born in summer is a tree in full leaf under a hot sky, green and generous and a little thirsty. You pour into the season: your birth season pulls your element outward, into expression. In love you show your feelings through what you do and make: gifts, plans, words, cooking, effort. Effort that goes unanswered is the thing that wears you down. Choose someone who responds in kind.

For Gap Wood in a relationship, this season shapes how quickly you commit and how much shade you give before you ask for any back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your effort is your love letter. Pick someone who reads it.

earth.intro:
Your Wood arrived in the Earth days that close a season: a tree with its roots wrapped around heavy soil. You shape the season: your element works on the season you were born in. In love that makes you a builder and a provider: you show commitment by creating stability, plans and a shared life with structure. You're excellent at the practical side of partnership. Make sure the romance gets a slot in the calendar too.

For Gap Wood in a relationship, this season shapes how quickly you commit and how much shade you give before you ask for any back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Builder in love. Put romance in the calendar too.

autumn.intro:
Picture Wood born in autumn: a tree in the season of the axe, when the air turns sharp and the leaves come down. The season tests you: the season you were born in presses on your element. In love that gave you a strong sense of duty and loyalty. You take commitment seriously and expect your partner to do the same. Lightness can be harder for you; let your partner make you laugh at yourself.

For Gap Wood in a relationship, this season shapes how quickly you commit and how much shade you give before you ask for any back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Loyal to the core. Let them make you laugh at yourself.

winter.intro:
Wood born in winter is a bare tree with its roots deep in cold, wet ground, quietly drinking. The season feeds you: your birth season feeds your element, and in love that shows up as someone who was well nourished early and knows how to nourish back. You're good at receiving care without feeling smothered, and you give it naturally. You may look for a partner who feels like home before anything else.

For Gap Wood in a relationship, this season shapes how quickly you commit and how much shade you give before you ask for any back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You know how to be cared for. Rare and lovely.

base.how-you-love:
Eul Wood loves like a climbing flower: you wrap yourself around the person you choose and grow toward them. You're romantic, attentive and charming, the partner who remembers the tiny details, the coffee order, the name of their childhood dog, the song from the second date.

Your love language is closeness. You want to be part of your partner's daily life: texting through the day, sharing friends, building a world that's 'ours'. You're adaptable, so you'll adjust to their schedule, their family, their habits, often more than you should.

The soft spot: you need to feel chosen, repeatedly. Vines need something to hold onto, and if your partner goes distant, you feel it in your whole body. Say when you need reassurance, before the worry starts steering you.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The climbing flower in love: you grow toward your person.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You remember their childhood dog's name. Of course you do.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Daily closeness is your love language.

base.how-you-love:
Byeong Fire loves like the sun: warm, generous, impossible to miss. When you're in love, everyone knows. You plan surprises, post the photos, introduce them to everyone and make ordinary weekends feel like holidays. Your partner feels celebrated.

Your love language is enthusiasm and quality time with energy in it: adventures, trips, dinners with friends, spontaneous plans. You give affection freely and expect it back with the same brightness. A partner who's lukewarm or hard to read can make you anxious, and you may turn up the heat to get a reaction.

The soft spot: you need appreciation. Suns shine without asking for thanks, but you do notice when nobody says the light was nice. Tell your partner what makes you feel loved, specifically.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: The sun in love: everyone knows, immediately.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Surprise trip, the photos, introductions to the entire city.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Celebrate them, and tell them how to celebrate you.

base.how-you-love:
Jeong Fire loves like a candle in a quiet room: intimate, steady and deeply attentive. You don't need grand gestures. You notice your partner's moods before they do, you remember what worried them last week, and you create a feeling of being truly understood that people rarely find twice.

Your love language is emotional intimacy: long talks, honest feelings, small rituals that belong only to the two of you. You give care generously and quietly. You also need to feel emotionally safe; carelessness or coldness can make your flame flicker for a long time.

The soft spot: you give more than you ask for. Candles burn themselves to give light. Make sure your partner knows how to look after you, because you'll rarely tell them unless they ask.

The soft spot: you rarely show vulnerability. Mountains look unshakable. Inside, you can be lonely if your partner never asks how you're really doing. Let them climb up and see the view from where you stand.
